labels.text: Describe a task or ask a question

S67.01.needs: a repository the GitHub app can reach (Cloud), or a Local folder on the desktop app
S67.01.note: Cloud runs need the sandbox switch the plan describes (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY, apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts); this was not checked live.
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar.
Click "Change repository" and choose a repository you can reach.
Type "Explain the structure of this repository: main parts, entry points and how they fit" and send it.
Check the reply names the main folders, the entry points and how they connect, as Expected says.
S67.01.where: Code (sidebar) > Change repository > pick a repository > type in "Describe a task or ask a question"

labels.text: Review the changes in this session for bugs

S67.20.needs: a session with changes in a repository (Cloud), or a Local session with changes
S67.20.note: On a Local session the same review is the "Review code" button in the changes panel (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts).
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar and open a session that has changes.
Click the composer, type "/" and choose "/review" ("Review the changes in this session for bugs").
Send it and wait for the reply.
Check the reply lists issues with file and line references.
S67.20.where: Code (sidebar) > open a session with changes > type "/review" in "Describe a task or ask a question"

S67.21.needs: a GitHub account with the app installed on a repository, and a pull request
S67.21.note: The review is posted on GitHub, not in the AGI screens; the GitHub card location was read from code, not seen live.
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors, then the GitHub card.
Turn on "Review pull requests" for the account you want.
Open a pull request in that repository on GitHub, or comment "@agi-workforce review" on it.
Check a review comment appears on the pull request with findings.
S67.21.where: Settings > Connectors > GitHub > "Review pull requests" (turn on for the account); or comment "@agi-workforce review" on a pull request in a connected repository on GitHub

labels.text: Search or type a branch name

S67.30.needs: a Cloud session with a repository
S67.30.note: The code checks out the typed branch; it was not confirmed that a missing name is created on the spot, and the agent can also be asked to create one in the composer.
steps: Open a Cloud session with a repository.
Click "Change the branch" and type a new branch name in "Search or type a branch name".
Click "Use branch".
Check the branch name shown in "Changes" is the new one.
S67.30.where: Code (sidebar) > open a Cloud session > "Change the branch" > type a new name in "Search or type a branch name" > "Use branch"

S67.31.needs: a GitHub account with the GitHub App installed, and a session whose branch has commits
S67.31.note: The pull request is opened as a draft (apps/web/lib/github-app.ts, buildPullRequestBody and draft option), which Expected does not mention.
steps: Click Code in the left sidebar.
Open a session that has a repository and a branch with commits.
Click Changes at the top of the session.
Click Create pull request. If it is greyed out, read the small text under it for the reason.
Look for a link to the new pull request on GitHub and a Checks status next to it, and compare with Expected.
S67.31.where: Code > open a session with a repository and a working branch > Changes > Create pull request

S67.33.needs: a GitHub account with the GitHub App installed, and a pull request with a failing check
S67.33.note: The investigation starts from a GitHub comment with @agi-workforce on the pull request (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts, the failing-checks prompt), not from a button in the app.
steps: Click Code in the left sidebar.
Open a session that already has a pull request.
Click Changes.
Look at the checks row. A failing run shows the Checks failing chip and the failed check names beside it. Click the refresh icon to reload.
Compare with Expected: the app only shows the failing checks; the investigation itself needs the GitHub mention in S67.34.
S67.33.where: Code > open a session with a pull request > Changes > Checks failing

S67.34.needs: an outside account (GitHub) with the GitHub App installed on a repository
S67.34.note: No Slack mention or in-app control for coding tasks was found; Slack appears only as an inbound trigger source in apps/web/lib/triggers with no screen.
steps: On GitHub, open an issue or pull request in a repository where the GitHub App is installed.
Write a comment that starts with @agi-workforce followed by a request, such as a bug to fix, and post it.
Wait for the reply comment from the app.
Check that the reply links to a Code session, and compare with Expected: the agent does the coding task from the mention.
S67.34.where: GitHub issue or pull request comment; the effect shows as a reply comment on GitHub
